nodes.title: Foundation: Adapter Alignment, Codegen Foundation, and Dead Code Removal
nodes.goal: Unblock all downstream work by aligning worm_postgres and worm_mongodb adapters to the post-EPIC-004 query/schema API, extending the build_runner generator to emit typed relation constants and process annotations, and deleting the duplicate Worm registry class so subsequent epics can build on a clean foundation.
workflows: W1-Adapter-Postgres-Rewrite: read current worm_postgres compiler → identify ~120 analyzer errors → rewrite compiler against new query/schema API → mix in ExplainCapable → run dart analyze until clean → run adapter contract harness

W2-Adapter-Mongo-Rewrite: read current worm_mongodb compiler → identify ~77 analyzer errors → rewrite against new API → mix in ExplainCapable using Mongo explain command → run dart analyze until clean → run adapter contract harness

W3-Contract-Harness-Restore: un-exclude lib/testing/adapter_contract.dart from analyzer → rewrite runAdapterContractTests(factory, capabilities) against current API → wire CI to run harness against InMemoryAdapter, worm_postgres, worm_mongodb

W4-Codegen-Relation-Constants: extend scope_generator/build_runner pipeline → for each @Table model emit User$ companion with RelationField<...> static constants (User$.posts, User$.profile) → ensure output is cast-free

W5-Codegen-Annotation-Readers: extend generator to surface @Hidden/@Appended/@Computed/@CastAs/@Fillable/@Guarded metadata as per-model descriptors that runtime consumers (Serializer, CastManager, Model.fillable/guarded) can read in EPIC-003

W6-Worm-Dedup: delete lib/src/registry/worm_registry.dart and test/src/registry/worm_registry_test.dart → audit imports for stale references → confirm registry barrel re-exports worm.dart only → run dart test 722/722
errorHandling: EH1: adapter compile failure → block PR merge via pre-merge gate; do not advance to dependent epics
EH2: contract harness fails on any adapter → fail CI with adapter name + failing contract method in error message
EH3: generator emits uncompilable code → build_runner reports error with model name and annotation context; no partial generation
EH4: removing worm_registry.dart breaks an import → grep for direct imports first; fail loudly rather than silently leaving a broken state
EH5: cast appears in generated code → generator self-test rejects output containing ' as ' patterns
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: dart analyze is clean in packages/worm_postgres and packages/worm_mongodb against current main
AC-2: runAdapterContractTests passes against InMemoryAdapter, worm_postgres, worm_mongodb in CI
AC-3: both adapter packages mix in ExplainCapable and respond to explain() calls
AC-4: build_runner emits User$.posts and User$.profile as typed RelationField constants for at least one test model, verified by a generated-code snapshot test
AC-5: generator output contains zero ' as ' casts (verified by string scan in generator test)
AC-6: lib/src/registry/worm_registry.dart and its test are deleted; only one final class Worm exists in lib/
AC-7: dart format / dart analyze / dart test pass cleanly in all four packages
AC-8: audit Executive Summary table flips Status from ⚠ to ✓ for EPIC-010, EPIC-023, EPIC-016 rows in same PR set
risks: Adapter rewrites touch every query path — high regression surface; mitigate via contract harness as the gate
Generator changes may emit subtly broken code that compiles but misbehaves at runtime; mitigate with executable snapshot tests
Hidden direct imports of worm_registry.dart elsewhere in monorepo may break on deletion
Mongo replica-set requirement for transactions not enforced at runtime; users on standalone Mongo may hit confusing errors

nodes.title: Exception Hierarchy Completion and Internal Reference Cleanup
nodes.goal: Round out the exception hierarchy with missing types (ConnectionTimeout, Authentication, CheckConstraint, Syntax, LazyLoading, MigrationLock, IrreversibleMigration, UnsupportedOperation, OperationCancelled), add umbrella types (ModelException, AdapterException), alias FullTableScanException ↔ DangerousQueryException, standardize error-context fields, and strip every WI-XXX / AC-N comment from lib/ and test/ while adding a lint rule preventing reintroduction. SPLIT DELIVERY: W1–W4 and W7 (exception type definitions) must ship before EPIC-001 through EPIC-005 so those epics throw properly-typed exceptions from day one; W5–W6 (comment sweep and lint rule) and W8 (ConfigurationException migration) run after all feature epics are complete.
workflows: W1-Missing-Exception-Types: add ConnectionTimeoutException, AuthenticationException, CheckConstraintException, SyntaxException, LazyLoadingException (used by EPIC-003 and EPIC-005), MigrationLockException, IrreversibleMigrationException, UnsupportedOperationException, OperationCancelledException — each with required context fields
W2-Umbrella-Types: introduce ModelException and AdapterException as abstract bases → existing concrete exceptions extend appropriate umbrella → catch sites can now catch broad categories
W3-Aliases: add FullTableScanException = DangerousQueryException typedef so spec name and code name both resolve
W4-Context-Standardization: ensure every exception carries table, column, query, migration, model fields where applicable; null when irrelevant; non-null when known
W5-WI-Comment-Sweep: grep lib/ and test/ for WI-001..WI-008 and AC-1..AC-10 patterns → delete each occurrence; replace with intent-described comment only when removing would confuse a future reader

W6-Lint-Rule: add custom analyzer rule (under packages/worm/lints/ or analysis_options.yaml include) rejecting any new WI-XXX or AC-N comment in lib/ or test/ → CI runs lint as part of dart analyze gate
W7-Construction-Tests: every new exception subtype has a construction-and-context test asserting all fields are populated and toString format is stable
W8-UnsupportedOperation-Migration: replace existing ConfigurationException throws for unsupported-by-adapter operations with UnsupportedOperationException(adapter, operation)
errorHandling: EH1: lint rule false positive on legitimate WI-mentioning string (e.g. test of the lint itself) → allow inline // ignore: directive only for the lint-test file
EH2: typedef alias must not break catch-by-type behavior; verified by test catching DangerousQueryException after typedef
EH3: existing catch sites that catch ConfigurationException for adapter operations must be updated to catch UnsupportedOperationException; grep-and-fix in same PR
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: each new exception subtype has a construction-and-context test passing
AC-2: ModelException is base of ValidationException, MassAssignmentException, others; AdapterException is base of ConnectionTimeoutException, AuthenticationException, etc.
AC-3: catch (e) where e is ModelException catches every model-layer exception
AC-4: FullTableScanException and DangerousQueryException are mutually catchable
AC-5: every exception's toString includes table/model/migration context when set
AC-6: grep for 'WI-' or 'AC-[0-9]' in lib/ and test/ returns zero results (or only allowed lint-test fixtures)
AC-7: custom lint rule fires on a deliberately-bad sample file; CI fails on its presence
AC-8: no UnsupportedOperationException sites still throw ConfigurationException for the same condition
AC-9: dart format / dart analyze / dart test pass cleanly post-cleanup
AC-10: audit row for EPIC-021 and EPIC-017 flipped to ✓ in same PR
risks: Adding umbrella types may shadow existing catch ordering if not paired with cleanup; sweep catch sites carefully
Lint rule may bounce on existing files until cleanup completes; run cleanup before enabling rule
typedef alias may not behave identically in all Dart versions for is-checks; verify behavior on minimum supported SDK
Standardizing context fields means changing existing exception constructors — minor breaking changes, justified at 0.x
W1–W4 must be extracted and shipped before feature epics begin to avoid placeholder exception types; coordinate split delivery explicitly

nodes.title: Model Lifecycle Finish-Out and Top-Level Transactions
nodes.goal: Complete the Active Record lifecycle by adding update/forceDelete/replicate/withoutEvents, auto-firing validation inside save(), wiring beforeRestore/afterRestore hooks, switching validation to typed Map<Field, List<ValidationRule>>, and shipping Worm.transaction with an adapter-state callback queue so afterCommit fires only on commit.
workflows: W1-Convenience-Methods: add Model.update(Map) as fill+save shortcut → lift Model.forceDelete() onto every Model (not just SoftDeletes) → implement Model.replicate({except:[...]}) returning unsaved deep copy with new ID
W2-Event-Muting: implement Model.withoutEvents(callback) and Model.withoutEvents([Type,...], callback) static muting; verify hooks suppressed inside callback and restored after

W3-Validation-Wiring: invoke Validator.validate inside Model.save between beforeValidate and afterValidate hooks → migrate rules getter from Validatable interface to Map<Field, List<ValidationRule>> on Model → add updateRules override for dirty-only validation → update every model + test in same PR
W4-Restore-Hooks: extend LifecycleEvent enum with beforeRestore/afterRestore → dispatch from SoftDeletes.restore() → assert ordering in tests

W5-Internal-State-Sealing: annotate Model.relations, Model.injectedFields, Model.state with @internal from package:meta or move behind package-private accessors → add typed getOriginal<T>(Field<T>) overload

W6-Transaction-Helper: implement Worm.transaction<T>((txn) async {...}) with optional connection: override → add Model.save(transaction:) and Model.delete(transaction:) propagation → add txn.savepoint(() async {}) gated by capabilities

W7-AfterCommit-Queue: add per-transaction callback queue to DatabaseAdapter state → Model.afterCommit enqueues instead of firing immediately → Worm.transaction drains queue on commit and discards on rollback → verify nested transactions only drain at outermost commit
errorHandling: EH1: validation failure inside save → throw ValidationException with offending Field keys; do not persist row; afterValidate not dispatched
EH2: replicate called on unsaved model → throw StateError with model + reason
EH3: withoutEvents callback throws → restore hook registration before re-raising; do not leave dispatcher in muted state
EH4: savepoint requested against adapter without SavepointCapability → throw UnsupportedOperationException with adapter name
EH5: transaction body throws → rollback adapter, discard afterCommit queue, propagate exception with context
EH6: Validator finds rule keyed to Field not on model → throw ConfigurationException naming the model + field
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: Model.update(map) persists changes and fires Save lifecycle hooks in expected order
AC-2: Model.forceDelete() exists on every Model and hard-deletes regardless of SoftDeletes mixin presence
AC-3: Model.replicate(except:[Field]) returns unsaved copy with new ID and excluded fields cleared
AC-4: Model.withoutEvents([User], callback) suppresses only User-typed hooks for callback duration
AC-5: Validator.validate fires automatically in save() between beforeValidate and afterValidate, proven by hook-order test
AC-6: rules getter returns Map<Field, List<ValidationRule>> on a sample model; old Validatable interface removed
AC-7: beforeRestore and afterRestore dispatch in correct order during SoftDeletes.restore()
AC-8: Model.relations / injectedFields / state are @internal or package-private; consumer code outside lib/ cannot access them
AC-9: Worm.transaction commits on success, rolls back on exception, supports nesting, drains afterCommit only on outermost commit (proven by 4 separate tests)
AC-10: Model.save(transaction: txn) routes all SQL through txn and is visible only after commit
risks: Validation API migration touches every existing model — large blast radius; freeze other changes during migration PR
afterCommit queue design must handle nested transactions, parallel transactions on different connections, and exception rollback — easy to get subtly wrong
Lifting forceDelete to every Model risks accidental hard-deletes by users who expected soft-delete to be the default; document loudly
Sealing public-but-internal model state may break downstream code that reached into Model.state; flag in changelog

nodes.title: QueryBuilder Surface Completion
nodes.goal: Bring QueryBuilder<T> to feature-complete parity with the spec: scalar aggregate terminals, streaming terminals, boolean composition, query inspection, where overloads, typed-generic withoutGlobalScope, adapter-context gates with AdapterMismatchException, and whereRaw escape hatch — all pushing computation down to the adapter rather than materializing rows.
workflows: W1-Scalar-Aggregates: add sum/avg/min/max terminals to QueryBuilder<T> that delegate to DatabaseAdapter.aggregate(...) → adapter pushes down to SQL/Mongo; never load rows in memory
W2-Streaming-Terminals: add stream() returning Stream<T>, chunk(size, callback) iterating in batches, streamChunks(size) returning Stream<List<T>> → verify constant memory on 50k-row test

W3-Boolean-Composition: implement whereGroup((q)=>q.where(...).orWhere(...)) compiling to parenthesized AND/OR group → whereExists<T>(subqueryBuilder) → whereColumn(left, right) for cross-column comparisons
W4-Query-Inspection: add toSql() rendering driver-specific SQL with placeholders, toMongoFilter() rendering Mongo filter doc, explain() returning ExplainPlan, debug() chainable logger hook
W5-Where-Overloads: add 2-arg where(field, value) (implicit eq) and 3-arg where(field, op, value) overloads; preserve existing builder-fn form
W6-Scope-Typing: implement withoutGlobalScope<X extends GlobalScope<T>>() reading X.name at compile time; deprecate string form

W7-Adapter-Gates: implement .sql((q) => q.join(...).having(...)) and .mongo((q) => q.rawFilter({...}).pipeline([...])) closures that throw AdapterMismatchException when called against wrong adapter; expose join/having on SqlQueryContext, rawFilter/pipeline on MongoQueryContext
W8-Raw-Escape: add whereRaw(sql, params, allowRaw: true) requiring explicit allowRaw to prevent accidental injection; documents Worm.unsafe pairing
errorHandling: EH1: sum/avg called on non-numeric column → throw TypeError at builder construction (compile-time via Field<num> generic) or runtime with field name
EH2: stream consumer cancels → adapter cursor closes; partial fetch logged at DEBUG
EH3: .sql() called on Mongo adapter → throw AdapterMismatchException(expected: 'sql', actual: 'mongo', operation: 'sql gate')
EH4: whereRaw without allowRaw: true → throw ConfigurationException with guidance to set allowRaw: true and ideally wrap in Worm.unsafe
EH5: explain() against adapter not mixing ExplainCapable → throw UnsupportedOperationException(adapter)
EH6: whereExists subquery returns no rows → outer predicate false; no exception
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: query.sum(field) emits adapter-side aggregate (verified via SQL trace) and does not iterate rows
AC-2: query.stream() over 50k rows holds < 50MB resident growth (perf regression test in EPIC-007)
AC-3: query.chunk(500, fn) calls fn with successive 500-row lists until exhausted; assertion test on synthetic dataset
AC-4: whereGroup produces parenthesized SQL ((a AND b) OR c) verified by toSql()
AC-5: whereExists subquery compiles to EXISTS (...) in SQL and $exists pipeline in Mongo
AC-6: query.where(field, value) is equivalent to query.where(field, Operator.eq, value)
AC-7: withoutGlobalScope<SoftDeletesScope>() compiles and bypasses scope without string lookup
AC-8: .sql() gate against InMemoryAdapter or worm_mongodb throws AdapterMismatchException with both adapter names in the message
AC-9: toSql() and toMongoFilter() return strings matching golden files for representative queries
AC-10: every public terminal has at least one execution test against InMemoryAdapter
risks: Streaming terminals require adapter cursor semantics that may differ wildly between Postgres, Mongo, and InMemoryAdapter; abstraction may leak
whereExists requires subquery compilation — easy to mis-scope generics
Adapter gates introduce a parallel chainable surface that must stay in sync with the main builder; risk of feature drift
whereRaw is an injection vector if allowRaw guard is bypassed; document loudly and ensure escape hatch only logs at WARN

nodes.title: Relations Runtime and Annotation Wiring
nodes.goal: Build on EPIC-000's codegen foundation to deliver typed relation accessors on Model instances (user.posts.add, user.roles.attach/sync/detach), constrained eager loading with nested paths, OnDelete.ormCascade runtime behavior, central morph-type registry, and wire every currently-unused annotation (@Hidden, @Appended, @Computed, @CastAs, @Fillable, @Guarded) into its runtime consumer plus ship DurationCast.
workflows: W1-Relation-Accessors: extend generator to emit per-relation accessor methods on Model instance (BelongsToAccessor, HasManyAccessor, BelongsToManyAccessor) wrapping PivotManager → expose add/dissociate for HasMany, attach/detach/sync for BelongsToMany
W2-Constrained-Eager: extend QueryBuilder.withRelation(RelationField, (q)=>q.where(...)) signature → eager loader applies filter to child query → cache filter per-relation key
W3-Nested-Paths: support User$.posts.include([Post$.comments]) syntax → generator emits include() on RelationField → eager loader walks path tree breadth-first batching at each level

W4-OrmCascade: implement OnDelete.ormCascade in Model.delete → before parent delete, walk declared cascading relations, recursively delete children via ORM (firing their hooks) → contrast with DB-level CASCADE which bypasses hooks
W5-Morph-Registry: replace per-relation polymorphic type maps with a central Worm.morphRegistry that resolves type strings ↔ Dart Types; relations consult registry on hydrate/persist
W6-Annotation-Hidden: Serializer reads per-model Hidden field list from codegen descriptor and skips listed fields in toMap/toJson
W7-Annotation-Appended-Computed: generator emits getter stubs for @Appended (DB-derived) and @Computed (transient); Serializer includes Appended in output, excludes Computed from SQL
W8-Annotation-CastAs: generator registers @CastAs(MyCast) entries into CastManager at model bootstrap; CastManager.put(field, MyCast()) called from generated code

W9-Annotation-Fillable-Guarded: generator overrides Model.fillable / Model.guarded lists from annotations; mass-assignment respects them; @experimental marker removed from these six annotations as their consumer ships
W10-DurationCast: implement DurationCast extends Cast<Duration, int> with toDatabase (inMilliseconds) and fromDatabase (Duration(milliseconds:)); add to default cast registry
errorHandling: EH1: relation accessor called on unloaded relation in strict mode → throw LazyLoadingException(model, relation)
EH2: attach/sync against pivot table with missing FK row → throw ConstraintViolationException with pivot table and missing FK
EH3: ormCascade encounters circular relation graph → detect cycle, throw ConfigurationException listing cycle path
EH4: morph type string not registered → throw ConfigurationException naming type string and suggesting Worm.morphRegistry.register
EH5: @CastAs targets non-existent Cast class → codegen fails with field + cast name; no runtime crash
EH6: @Hidden on field that does not exist on model → generator error with model + field name
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: user.posts.add(post) persists post with FK set; user.posts list reflects new post on next access
AC-2: user.roles.sync([1,2,3]) results in exactly those 3 pivot rows; previous rows for 4 are deleted; test asserts pivot table state
AC-3: query.withRelation(User$.posts, (q) => q.where(Post$.published, true)) loads only published posts into parent eager-load result
AC-4: query.with(User$.posts.include([Post$.comments])) loads 2-level deep with exactly 3 queries (users, posts, comments)
AC-5: deleting parent with OnDelete.ormCascade fires beforeDelete/afterDelete on every child; verified by hook-order test
AC-6: Worm.morphRegistry resolves 'post' ↔ Post for at least 2 distinct relations sharing the registry
AC-7: @Hidden field absent from toMap output
AC-8: @Computed field present in toMap but absent from generated SQL INSERT
AC-9: @CastAs(DurationCast) round-trips Duration ↔ ms integer through DB; null/zero/max-value tested
AC-10: @Fillable/@Guarded enforce mass-assignment; MassAssignmentException carries offending keys
risks: Relation accessors require generator and runtime to agree on signatures — drift between EPIC-000 generator output and runtime expectations
ormCascade hook ordering interacts with transactions; afterCommit fix from EPIC-001 must be solid before ormCascade ships
Annotation wiring touches Serializer + CastManager + mass-assignment all at once; isolated tests per annotation reduce blast radius
Central morph registry is global mutable state (sanctioned by constitution but still risky); needs reset hook for tests

nodes.title: Factory, Seeder, and CLI/Migration Enhancements
nodes.goal: Round out the developer experience layer: expose faker on Factory base, add count/create/has/for_/sequence methods, persist factory results, implement seeder tracking via worm_seeders table, add Worm.beginTestTransaction/rollbackTestTransaction, wire DiffEngine into worm make:migration --auto, enforce migration dependsOn ordering, honor schema:dump --prune, extend IndexDefinition with composite FKs and partial-unique indexes, and introduce the user-facing Schema facade so Migration.up accepts Schema rather than DatabaseAdapter.
workflows: W1-Factory-Surface: add faker getter on Factory base class exposing FakerService → add .count(n) chainable building n instances → .create([overrides]) persisting via Model.save → .has(otherFactory, RelationField) attaching children → .for_(parent, RelationField) setting FK on parent → .sequence([{...},{...}]) cycling overrides per instance

W2-Seeder-Tracking: create worm_seeders framework migration (id, name, batch, ran_at) → SeederRunner queries SeederRecordStore before running each seeder; skips if already recorded → records on success with batch number → add Seeder.order int for explicit ordering → introduce DatabaseSeeder master pattern that calls other seeders in declared order

W3-Test-Transaction: implement Worm.beginTestTransaction() opening a transaction on the default connection and binding it to a Zone-local or static field → rollbackTestTransaction() rolls back and clears binding → adapter routes all queries through this transaction during test

W4-Make-Migration-Auto: wire DiffEngine into worm make:migration <name> --auto CLI → diff currently-known model schema vs database schema → emit migration file with up/down using the diff output → --pretend prints diff without writing
W5-Schema-Dump-Prune: implement --prune on worm schema:dump → squash old migrations into a single baseline; mark squashed migrations as run in worm_migrations; keep recent migrations as-is
W6-DependsOn-Ordering: extend Migration base with List<Type> dependsOn → MigrationRunner topologically sorts before running; throws ConfigurationException on cycle naming both migrations

W7-Index-Extensions: extend IndexDefinition with composite foreign keys (List<Field> for parent + child) and partial-unique index predicate (e.g. UNIQUE WHERE deleted_at IS NULL); generator + Blueprint expose builder syntax

W8-Migration-Schema-Facade: introduce user-facing Schema facade; wrap Migration.up(DatabaseAdapter) to accept Schema facade matching spec; keep legacy Migration.up(DatabaseAdapter) as an overload during transition; migration template uses Schema, not SchemaDescriptor
errorHandling: EH1: factory.create() on transient model → reuses Worm.unsafe(transient) path if model not registered; otherwise throws ConfigurationException
EH2: seeder runs against database without worm_seeders table → log warning, skip tracking, run anyway; instruct user to run framework migration
EH3: dependsOn cycle → throw ConfigurationException listing the cycle path
EH4: make:migration --auto with no diff → exit 0, print 'no changes detected'; do not write empty file
EH5: schema:dump --prune with active uncommitted migrations → throw, refuse to prune until migrations are flushed
EH6: Worm.beginTestTransaction called twice without rollback → throw StateError naming the active txn
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: UserFactory().count(5).create() persists 5 rows and returns List<User>
AC-2: UserFactory().has(PostFactory().count(3), User$.posts).create() persists 1 user + 3 posts with FKs set
AC-3: UserFactory().sequence([{name:'a'},{name:'b'}]).count(4).create() produces 4 users alternating names a,b,a,b
AC-4: factory.faker.firstName() returns deterministic value when Worm.seedRandom(42) is set
AC-5: running same seeder twice records 1 row in worm_seeders and skips on second invocation
AC-6: DatabaseSeeder.run() calls its child seeders in declared order; verified by recording order in a fake
AC-7: Worm.beginTestTransaction + rollbackTestTransaction leaves database in pre-test state; verified by row count
AC-8: worm make:migration --auto generates migration file matching detected diff; round-trips back to clean diff after running
AC-9: dependsOn cycle is rejected with both migration names in the error
AC-10: composite FK and partial-unique index appear in generated DDL for at least one adapter test
AC-11: Migration.up(Schema) compiles and executes correctly; legacy Migration.up(DatabaseAdapter) overload still accepted without deprecation warning
risks: Test transaction binding mechanism (Zone vs static) affects parallel test isolation; pick deterministic approach and document
DiffEngine wiring may surface bugs in DiffEngine itself that were latent; budget for diff fixes
schema:dump --prune is destructive; require --force in non-dev environments per constitution UX rule
Composite FK syntax must work for both Postgres and Mongo (Mongo treats composite FKs differently); abstraction must accommodate or explicitly throw
Schema facade changes Migration.up signature; document manual migration path for user projects in changelog

nodes.title: Strictness, Scopes, and Spec API Aliases
nodes.goal: Make strict mode genuinely enforceable: auto-apply @GlobalScope on every QueryBuilder via codegen extensions, generate typed scope extension methods (not just List<String>), throw on lazy-loading in strict mode, enforce preventFullTableScans on .get() without .where(), unify preventFullTableScans/preventDestructiveWithoutWhere overlap, and provide spec-name aliases (Operator.equals, whereIn, table.id(), cursorPaginate(after:)) so spec examples compile literally. Schema facade compatibility (Migration.up accepting Schema) is delivered by EPIC-004 W8 and is a prerequisite for this epic.
workflows: W1-Scope-AutoApply: extend codegen to emit per-model QueryBuilder extension applying all @GlobalScope-tagged scopes by default → withoutGlobalScope<X>() removes one → withoutGlobalScopes() removes all
W2-Scope-Extension-Methods: generator emits callable extension methods for each LocalScope (e.g. query.published() for PublishedScope) instead of only List<String> scopeNames
W3-Lazy-Load-Prevention: in strict mode, accessing a relation that was not eager-loaded throws LazyLoadingException(model, relation) → can be bypassed inside Worm.unsafe(()=>...)
W4-Full-Scan-Prevention: in strict mode, query.get() / first() without any .where() throws DangerousQueryException(query) → bypass inside Worm.unsafe

W5-Strictness-Unification: pick canonical flag (preventDestructiveWithoutWhere covers update/delete; preventFullTableScans covers read) → document distinction in constitution → remove overlapping behavior
W6-Operator-Aliases: add Operator.equals, notEquals, greaterThan, lessThan, greaterThanOrEqual, lessThanOrEqual as static const pointers to short forms
W7-Field-Operator-Aliases: add whereIn, whereNotIn, whereBetween, whereNotBetween, whereLike, whereNotLike on FieldOperators extension
W8-Blueprint-Aliases: add table.id() (UUID primary), table.intId() (auto-incr int primary), table.uuid(name) helpers on Blueprint
W9-Pagination-Alias: support cursorPaginate(perPage:, after:) parameter name (alias for current cursor:); rename Page.data → items, hasMorePages → hasNextPage + hasPrevPage where spec example demands
errorHandling: EH1: LazyLoadingException thrown outside Worm.unsafe → message includes model name, relation name, suggestion to eager-load
EH2: DangerousQueryException thrown for .get() without .where() in strict mode → message includes table name and stack trace pointer
EH3: scope auto-application encounters duplicate scope names → generator-time error naming both scopes
EH4: spec alias used (e.g. Operator.equals) routes to Operator.eq with zero runtime overhead — purely compile-time pointer
EH5: cursorPaginate(after: X, cursor: Y) called with both → throw ArgumentError naming both params
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: every QueryBuilder<User> automatically applies User's @GlobalScope-tagged scopes; bypass with withoutGlobalScope<X>()
AC-2: generator emits query.published() for a PublishedScope LocalScope; calling it adds the scope's where clause
AC-3: accessing user.posts when not eager-loaded throws LazyLoadingException in strict mode and returns lazy load in non-strict mode
AC-4: User.query().get() (no .where()) throws DangerousQueryException in strict mode
AC-5: Worm.unsafe wraps a callback that performs an otherwise-blocked .get() and succeeds
AC-6: Operator.equals === Operator.eq (identical instance, compile-time alias)
AC-7: field.whereIn([1,2,3]) and field.inList([1,2,3]) both compile and produce same query
AC-8: blueprint.id() declares UUID primary key; blueprint.intId() declares auto-incr int primary key
AC-9: cursorPaginate(perPage: 10, after: 'abc') returns CursorPage<T> identical to cursorPaginate(perPage: 10, cursor: 'abc')
risks: Auto-applied scopes can mask data the user expected to see; document loudly that scopes are always-on unless bypassed
Renaming Page<T>.data → items breaks every caller; weigh against 0.x blessing — prefer alias over rename
Strict-mode enforcement may break existing well-written tests that did not anticipate strictness; ship strict mode off by default and document opt-in
Schema facade migration is owned by EPIC-004; this epic must not ship until EPIC-004 W8 is merged

nodes.title: Performance Optimizations, Adapter Integration, and E2E Testing
nodes.goal: Land the cross-cutting performance and quality work: lazy attribute hydration scoped to select([...]) columns, concurrent eager-load relation fetching via Future.wait, IN-chunking at 1000 IDs in all adapters, full E2E CLI workflow tests (empty project → init → make:model → migrate → db:seed → query), and a performance regression suite enforcing 10k inserts < 5s, 1k+5k batched eager-load < 500ms with exactly 2 queries, 50k streamed rows < 50MB resident growth.
workflows: W1-Lazy-Hydration: when query uses select([fieldA, fieldB]) only those columns populate the model; unselected columns marked 'not loaded' → accessing unloaded field throws or returns sentinel based on strictness → refresh(select:[...]) re-fetches additional columns
W2-Concurrent-Eager-Load: in eager_loader, group independent relations and dispatch via Future.wait → dependent relations serialize naturally → verify against parallel-safe test fixtures
W3-IN-Chunking: every adapter chunks IN clauses at 1000 IDs → InMemoryAdapter, worm_postgres, worm_mongodb each implement → contract test verifies behavior on 1500-ID input

W4-E2E-CLI-Workflows: create test/e2e/ harness that spawns CLI in temp directory → runs init → make:model User → make:migration → migrate → make:seeder → db:seed → executes a Dart program that queries User → asserts row count → tears down
W5-Perf-Tier-Insert: benchmark 10k single-row inserts on InMemoryAdapter; threshold 5s wall-clock; track in benchmark/insert_throughput.dart with golden timing baseline
W6-Perf-Tier-Eager: benchmark 1k parents + 5k children via batched eager loader; assert exactly 2 adapter queries; threshold 500ms
W7-Perf-Tier-Stream: benchmark query.stream() over 50k rows; sample resident memory at 10% intervals; assert peak growth < 50MB
W8-Perf-Tier-Dirty-Update: benchmark dirty UPDATE for a row with 3 dirty fields out of 30; assert SQL touches only 3 columns via adapter trace
W9-Slow-Query-Budget: enforce slowQueryThreshold default 200ms; emit WARN log with rendered SQL + params when exceeded; verify in unit test
W10-NPlusOne-Strict-Mode: in strict mode, NPlusOneDetector warning escalates to thrown DangerousQueryException; integration test confirms
errorHandling: EH1: accessing an unselected column on a lazily-hydrated model in strict mode → throw FieldNotLoadedException(model, field) with refresh() suggestion
EH2: eager-load Future.wait failure on any relation → cancel siblings (best-effort), aggregate errors into RelationLoadException listing failed relations
EH3: IN-chunk fails partway → adapter reports which chunk failed; remaining chunks not run; caller decides retry
EH4: E2E test process times out (CLI hangs) → kill subprocess after 30s, report stdout/stderr
EH5: perf threshold exceeded in CI → fail build with measured value vs threshold and 3 most recent baseline values for context
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: query.select([User$.id, User$.name]).first() hydrates only id and name; accessing User$.email throws or returns sentinel in strict mode
AC-2: eager-loader runs independent relations concurrently; measured wall time < sequential lower bound on synthetic test
AC-3: IN-clause chunking verified at 1000-ID boundary for InMemoryAdapter, worm_postgres, worm_mongodb via contract test
AC-4: E2E test runs full CLI workflow end-to-end with non-zero row count at end and exits 0
AC-5: 10k inserts complete in < 5s on InMemoryAdapter (CI machine baseline)
AC-6: 1k+5k batched eager-load completes in < 500ms with exactly 2 adapter queries
AC-7: 50k row stream peaks at < 50MB resident growth
AC-8: dirty UPDATE on 3 dirty fields emits SQL touching only 3 columns (verified by adapter trace)
AC-9: query exceeding slowQueryThreshold logs WARN with SQL + params
AC-10: NPlusOneDetector in strict mode throws DangerousQueryException; non-strict mode logs WARN
risks: Lazy hydration interacts subtly with serialization and eager loading; need clear semantics for 'not loaded' vs null
Future.wait can mask individual relation failures; aggregation must preserve original errors
Perf thresholds vary by CI machine — pin to a reference baseline or use relative regression detection
E2E tests spawning subprocesses can be flaky in CI; use deterministic temp dirs and tight timeouts
Memory measurement in Dart is approximate (no exact RSS API); use ProcessInfo.currentRss with documented variance
